Appearance:

sentences.text: By this application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the applicant - original accused no. 4 Yakub Patel, seeks to invoke inherent powers of this Court praying for quashment of FIR being I.CR. No 47 of 2014, registered with Kausamba Police Station, Surat (Rural), for the offences punishable under Section 406, 420 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code.

2. Facts and circumstances giving rise to file present application are that, the complainant second respondent being a business manager, associated with Air Communication, lodged an FIR for the offence of criminal breach of trust and cheating against five persons.
The Air Communication was having a distributorship of Samsung TV over the jurisdictional area of Surat City and Rural area.
The accused nos. 1 and 2 were in business of Electronic Items doing business in the name and style 'National Electronical' at Surat.
Due to business relations, the accused nos. 1 and 2 purchased Samsung TV worth Rs.7,84,618/- on credit basis.

It is alleged that, the accused nos. 1 and 2 had hatched the conspiracy to cheat the complainant, as a result, they had placed the purchase order and after receiving the goods, they had Yakubbhai Hajiumarji Patel vs State Of Gujarat

1 sold it again to accused no. 4 - the present applicant herein, who was also part of the alleged conspiracy and in connivance of the co-accused, he was financially benefited.
It is further alleged in the FIR that, the accused no. 1 had issued two cheques towards due amount of business transaction and out of two, one cheque of Rs.4,02,508/- was dishonoured.

It is alleged that, despite their inability to pay the purchase price, they have misused the trust of the complainant and after receiving the goods, in collusion with the co-accused, same was disposed of in the open market and obtained the money and did not pay the same to the respondent complainant, whereby, the accused have committed an offence of criminal breach of trust and cheating with an intention to dishonestly induces the complainant to deliver the goods.
3.
In the aforesaid facts, the FIR came to be filed against the accused for the offences as referred above.
The applicant herein being accused no.4, has preferred present application, for quashing of the FIR, mainly on the ground that, the dispute herein appears to be civil in nature.

The R/CR.MA/4141/2014 ORDER DATED: 20/04/2023 applicant herein being a dealer of Electronic goods, had purchased the TV / LED, from the accused no. 1 - National Electronical and had paid the purchase price including the tax to the accused no. 1
and same is reflected in his accounts.

Thus,
there was no fault on the part of the applicant accused as he had not directly placed an order with the respondent complainant and as such, the basic requirement of entrustment of the property is not established.
4. Mr. Dipak Sindhi, learned counsel appearing for and on behalf of the applicant accused submitted that, the civil dispute has been given a clock of criminal proceedings.

The applicant is doing his business in the name and style 'Paras Electronics' and having nothing to do with the business transactions entered into between the accused nos. 1 and 2 and respondent complainant.
He has urged that, the applicant had purchased the goods from the accused nos. 1 and 2 through bank transactions and official entry / transaction was also reflected in the accounts.

Thus, it was official transaction between the accused no. 1 and applicant and therefore, he has been falsely implicated in the alleged offence so as to pressurize him to settle the due amount of business transaction, which amount to misuse of process of law and court and therefore, the allegations leveled in the FIR if accepted, as it is, then also, no offence of cheating and criminal breach of trust are made out against the applicant herein.
R/CR.MA/4141/2014 ORDER DATED: 20/04/2023 5.

On the other hand, Mr. N.R. Kodekar and Mr. L.B. Dabhi, the learned State Counsel, have vehemently opposed the application and contended that, the applicant was the part of criminal conspiracy hatched by the accused no.1 and 2 and it is evident that, instead of purchasing the goods from the official distributors, he contacted the accused no.1 and 2 which is evident that he colluded with the principal accused and obtained financial benefits.

Thus, when there is a specific allegation leveled against the applicant that he was involved in the alleged offence, the High Court will not be justified in embarking upon an enquiry as to the reliability or genuineness or otherwise of the allegations made in the FIR.
In such circumstances, it is submitted that, the application is misconceived and liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: 6. Having considered the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the respective parties and upon perusal of the allegations leveled in the FIR, the issue falls for my consideration is whether the applicant has made out a case for quashing of FIR?

7. Heard at length the learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the allegations leveled in the FIR.
8.
It is no doubt true that, prior to the registration of the FIR, the applicant herein did not have business relations with the respondent complainant.
He had purchased the goods from the accused no.1 and paid the purchase price to R/CR.MA/4141/2014 ORDER DATED: 20/04/2023 accused no.1.
The entire transaction reflected in the day to day books of accounts maintained in the regular course of business.
It needs to be noted that, the accused no. 1 had also issued invoices of the purchased goods in the name of 'Paras Electronics'.
The applicant has been charged with the act of criminal conspiracy.

It is settled law that association of the applicant with the main accused would not make him member of criminal conspiracy as meeting of mind is the essential to establish the factum of criminal conspiracy.

In the facts of the present case, the applicant entered into official business transaction for purchasing the LED TVs., which fact itself would not sufficient to infer that he was member of the alleged conspiracy and there was meeting of mind to do alleged offence of criminal breach of trust and cheating.
9.
For the foregoing reasons, this Court is of the prima-facie opinion that, in order to exert pressure upon the accused no.1 and 2, the present applicant herein has been arraigned as accused.
The law is well settled that, the criminal proceedings are not to be misused for settling the score or pressurizing the parties to settle the dispute.
The applicant herein, never purchased any goods from the respondent complainant, and it is not the case of the complainant that he had supplied the goods to the applicant.
There is no sufficient evidence in the form of invoices or otherwise to establish the ingredients to criminal conspiracy against the applicant herein.

The accusation made against the applicant herein, even if R/CR.MA/4141/2014 ORDER DATED: 20/04/2023 taken at face value and accepted in their entirety, do not constitute any offence against the applicant.

The case is fully covered by categories 1 and 7 as enumerated by Apex Court in case of Bhajanlal (1992) Supl. 1, 335)
and therefore, this Court is of the considered view that to prevent the abuse of process of law and court, this is a fit case to exercise inherent powers to quash the questioned FIR.
10. Resultantly, present application is allowed.

The impugned FIR being I.CR. No 47 of 2014,
registered with Kausamba Police Station, Surat (Rural), and consequential proceedings arising therefrom against present applicant is hereby quashed and set aside.
Direct service permitted.
(ILESH J. VORA,J) P.S. JOSHI Yakubbhai Hajiumarji Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121940647/
